questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find off campus housing through companies such as Hugo and Scape.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Beware if you study at the Monash Law Chambers that it is located in CBD, so you should find a place to live in that area, and not in Clayton, where the main campus is.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was all online and there where a lot of guides available through the Monash website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guides online on the Monash website and people who could assist you via e-mail from Monash Abroad.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and that fitted my schedule perfectly. I was also able to change a class during my exchange, because the exam didn't fit my schedule.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the Monash Abroad website, as it contains everything you need to know.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were a lot easier than at the University of Copenhagen. Most exams where done online from home, and consisted of papers which you had days if not weeks to write, on not very complicated subjects. You didn't need to know much about Australian Law either. The classes where easy to follow even though I didn't take any introduction classes to Australian Law.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is similar, but the students are more engaged at Monash. Maybe because they are sometimes graded for what they say in class, and because grades aren't anonymous. Or maybe because they pay to study there. The teachers where very experienced lawyers, who could start intense class discussions, and people where very eager to participate. There were no lectures, only seminars - which is similar to how you are taught during your masters at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Planning and Environmental Law
Intellectual Property
Regulating Shareholder Activism
Principles of Family Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I thought that Regulating Shareholder Activism was a great class. The teacher had a lot of knowledge on the subject, and used teaching methods that he has been taught at Harvard Law School. So there were a lot of class discussions and also in-class visits from professionals who work with shareholder activism in different ways. Although the exam form seemed more difficult than the rest of my classes, since it contained grades for participation and an in-class quiz, it wasn't too difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of furnishing your apartment, since most places don't come with any duvets, sheets, pillows, dishes, cleaning supplies etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I thought. However, no one at Monash spent any money on books, as they were all free online for students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most clubs where available, but it was all located at Clayton, so if you go to Law Chambers, that is about an hour away.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Running clubs in Melbourne!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Uluru - it was everyone's favorite experience during exchange. Also Tasmania and a road trip up the east coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is a very multi cultural city, so I don't know if I ever completely adjusted to it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Download WhatsApp.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the language barrier challenging. It was difficult to understand local Australian people who speak very fast. Especially some of the professors, when the legal jargon in-class is too complex.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Link up with all the Danish students one of your first days there.
Find a place to live from home - either rent through the FairyFloss group on Facebook or stay at Yugo or Scape.
Bring an empty suitcase.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you study law, only take master classes, so you have classes at Law Chambers located in CBD, as opposed to bachelor classes, which take place at Clayton in the suburbs. Be prepared that a lot of students at Monash are not Australian, and use ChatGPT to translate during class. So class is not where you will make friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people from my home university that I formed bonds with while abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from Denmark and being in such a multicultural city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
